expectation: Granular cytoplasmic GZMB in scattered single cytotoxic T and NK cells, usually rare. In gut-like mucosa they should sit in the lamina propria and between epithelial cells (intraepithelial lymphocytes), and on a subset of CD8a+ cells.
observed: A: glow follows tissue architecture (villi, epithelium, muscle) with stripes and a slide-wide glow. B/C: broad haze over the stroma and epithelium, no distinct cells. D: blurry haze plus one blob. E1 is haze; E3 has sparse green specks not on CD8a cells.
why: The signal follows tissue texture and autofluorescence, not a distinct cell population, and it does not sit on the CD8a+ cells.
notes: GZMB looks like tissue autofluorescence: haze over the villi and stroma, stripes and glow off the tissue, and no stained granular cells at any scale. In row E it does not sit on the CD8a+ cells.
